text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.7% today after climbing sharply over the previous three trading days, reaching $154 on Thursday. The pullback comes as crude oil prices dropped for a second consecutive day—U.S. crude fell below $104 per barrel—on growing hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the Iran conflict, even though U.S. military strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island occurred just this morning. When oil prices retreat, exploration and production companies like ConocoPhillips typically see their stock prices weaken, since their profits depend heavily on higher crude prices.

The broader context is mixed for the sector: while competitors like BP and Saudi Aramco posted outsized profits this quarter from surging refining margins (the difference between crude prices and refined product prices), ConocoPhillips is primarily an upstream producer and doesn't benefit as directly from those refining tailwinds. The stock's sharp $4 drop from Thursday's high suggests investors were betting on continued geopolitical risk premiums in oil—premiums that appear to be eroding as negotiation signals improve.
